claim: Motile Pseudomonas aeruginosa induce a specific gene expression program upon hitting a host cell.
source: Here, we employed a dual-sequencing approach to unravel conversational turn-taking of dynamic host–pathogen communications. We demonstrate that upon hitting a host cell, motile Pseudomonas aeruginosa induce a specific gene expression program.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this finding based on the dual-sequencing approach employed in the study.

claim: Motile Pseudomonas aeruginosa express spermidine on the surface upon host-cell contact.
source: We demonstrate that upon hitting a host cell, motile Pseudomonas aeruginosa induce a specific gene expression program. This results in the expression of spermidine on the surface, which specifically activates the PIP3-pathway to induce phagocytic uptake into primary or immortalized murine cells.
evidence: The abstract explicitly describes this as a result of the gene expression program induced upon host-cell contact.

claim: Spermidine specifically activates the PIP3-pathway to induce phagocytic uptake into primary or immortalized murine cells.
source: This results in the expression of spermidine on the surface, which specifically activates the PIP3-pathway to induce phagocytic uptake into primary or immortalized murine cells.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this mechanism based on experimental findings.

claim: Non-motile bacteria are more immunogenic due to a lower expression of arnT upon host-cell contact.
source: Non-motile bacteria are more immunogenic due to a lower expression of arnT upon host-cell contact, but do not produce spermidine and are phagocytosed less.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this finding comparing non-motile to motile bacteria.

claim: Non-motile bacteria do not produce spermidine.
source: Non-motile bacteria are more immunogenic due to a lower expression of arnT upon host-cell contact, but do not produce spermidine and are phagocytosed less.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this characteristic of non-motile bacteria.

claim: Non-motile bacteria are phagocytosed less than motile bacteria.
source: Non-motile bacteria are more immunogenic due to a lower expression of arnT upon host-cell contact, but do not produce spermidine and are phagocytosed less.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this finding based on experimental observations.

claim: Bacterial motility is linked to a host-cell-induced expression of additional immune modulators.
source: We demonstrate that not only the presence of pathogen inherent molecular patterns induces immune responses, but that bacterial motility is linked to a host-cell-induced expression of additional immune modulators.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this conclusion from the study.

claim: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is a major cause of infection in patients with underlying or immunocompromising conditions.
source: The problematic opportunistic pathogen Pseudomonas aeruginosa is a major cause of infection in patients with underlying or immunocompromising conditions.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: Therapeutic options of P. aeruginosa infections are increasingly limited due to the continued rise in antimicrobial resistances.
source: Therapeutic options of P. aeruginosa infections are increasingly limited due to the continued rise in antimicrobial resistances (Moradali et al., 2017; Streeter et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: P. aeruginosa has the ability to build biofilms and persist in the lungs of cystic fibrosis patients.
source: Furthermore, the ability of the pathogen to build biofilms and to persist e.g. in the lungs of cystic fibrosis (CF) patients facilitates the establishment of chronic infections, which are largely recalcitrant to antimicrobial therapies.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about P. aeruginosa.

claim: Bacteria express pathogen-associated molecular patterns (PAMPs) such as LPS or flagella.
source: Bacteria express pathogen-associated molecular patterns (PAMPs) such as LPS or flagella (Janssens and Beyaert, 2003; Molloy, 2013; Mukherjee et al., 2016; Park et al., 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to previous literature.

claim: Recognition of PAMPs by pattern recognition receptors (PRR) induces a strong inflammatory response to kill the pathogen.
source: Their recognition by specific host receptors called pattern recognition receptors (PRR) induces a strong inflammatory response to kill the pathogen.
evidence: This is stated as established immunological knowledge.

claim: Flagella are essentially required for the bacterium to reach target sites in the host and to establish an infection.
source: Flagella are essentially required for the bacterium to reach target sites in the host and to establish an infection (Duan et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The flagellum is recognized by toll-like receptor 5 (TLR5) or intracellular NLRC4 as a PAMP.
source: However, the flagellum is also recognized by toll-like receptor 5 (TLR5) or intracellular NLRC4 as a PAMP, thereby limiting bacterial establishment of an infection (Haasken and Sutterwala, 2013; Yoon et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: P. aeruginosa strains lacking a functional flagellum undergo less phagocytosis and are more resistant to clearance in vitro and in vivo.
source: P. aeruginosa strains lacking a functional flagellum have been demonstrated to undergo less phagocytosis and are more resistant to clearance in vitro and in vivo (Amiel et al., 2010; Lovewell et al., 2014; Lovewell et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The lower phagocytosis rate of non-motile strains was explained by diminished activation of the phosphatidylinositol-(3,4,5)-triphosphate (PIP3) pathway in host cells.
source: The lower phagocytosis rate of these non-motile strains was explained by diminished activation of the phosphatidylinositol-(3,4,5)-triphosphate (PIP3) pathway in host cells (Demirdjian et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The ΔfliC mutant is non-motile and does not produce a flagellum due to the lack of FliC molecules.
source: In addition to the PA14 wild-type we obtained: (i) a ΔfliC mutant, which is non-motile and does not produce a flagellum due to the lack of FliC molecules that build up the filament as the major extracellular part of the flagellum
evidence: This describes the characteristics of the ΔfliC mutant used in the study.

claim: The ΔflgK mutant is non-motile and does not produce a flagellum but secretes monomeric FliC molecules that function as PAMPs.
source: (ii) a ΔflgK mutant, which is non-motile and does not produce a flagellum but secretes monomeric FliC molecules that function as PAMPs (Gillen and Hughes, 1991)
evidence: This describes the characteristics of the ΔflgK mutant, supported by a citation.

claim: The ΔmotABCD mutant has a flagellum but is non-motile due to the lack of motor proteins.
source: (iii) a ΔmotAB ΔmotCD mutant (denoted as ΔmotABCD), which has a flagellum (recognized by the pattern recognition receptors (PRRs)), but is non-motile due to the lack of motor proteins (Toutain et al., 2005)
evidence: This describes the characteristics of the ΔmotABCD mutant, supported by a citation.

claim: All bacterial strains displayed the expected phenotypes in scanning electron microscopy and motility assays.
source: All bacterial strains displayed the expected phenotypes in scanning electron microscopy and motility assays (Figure 1).
evidence: This statement refers to experimental validation shown in Figure 1.

claim: The phagocytic uptake of all three motility mutants was significantly reduced as compared to PA14 in primary BMDMs.
source: The phagocytic uptake of all three motility mutants was significantly reduced as compared to PA14 in primary BMDMs (Figure 2A)
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The phagocytic uptake of all three motility mutants was significantly reduced as compared to PA14 in RAW264.7 macrophages.
source: The phagocytic uptake of all three motility mutants was significantly reduced as compared to PA14 in primary BMDMs (Figure 2A), in RAW264.7 macrophages (Figure 2B)
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The phagocytic uptake of all three motility mutants was significantly reduced as compared to PA14 in J774 cells.
source: The phagocytic uptake of all three motility mutants was significantly reduced as compared to PA14 in primary BMDMs (Figure 2A), in RAW264.7 macrophages (Figure 2B) and in J774 cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A – 1C).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A-1C.

claim: Introduction of fliC in trans restored flagella production, motility, and phagocytic uptake in the fliC deletion mutant to wild-type levels.
source: Introduction of fliC in trans restored flagella production, motility, and phagocytic uptake in the fliC deletion mutant to wild-type levels (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Addition of 10 µM cytochalasin D to the culture medium blocked bacterial uptake to less than 1%.
source: Addition of 10 µM cytochalasin D to the culture medium blocked bacterial uptake to less than 1% (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D – 1F).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D-1F.

claim: The adherence of the ΔfliC and ΔflgK strains to the cell surface of RAW264.7 macrophages was comparable to that of the wild-type PA14 strain.
source: The adherence of the ΔfliC and ΔflgK strains to the cell surface of RAW264.7 macrophages and of J774 cells was comparable to that of the wild-type PA14 strain (Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C)
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The flagellated, non-motile ΔmotABCD mutant adhered to the macrophages to a lesser extent.
source: Of note, the flagellated, non-motile ΔmotABCD mutant adhered to the macrophages to a lesser extent, indicating that the presence of a non-functional flagella might disturb close contact between the bacteria and the host cells (Laventie et al., 2019).
evidence: This observation is stated in the text and supported by a citation.

claim: Both non-motile clinical isolates were phagocytosed at lower rates by macrophages in comparison to the motile clinical isolate.
source: In line with the results for the PA14 strain, both non-motile clinical isolates were phagocytosed at lower rates by macrophages (Figure 2E) in comparison to the motile clinical isolate.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: The ΔmotABCD exhibited a differential expression of 206 genes as compared to PA14 under standard LB culture conditions.
source: While the ΔmotABCD exhibited a differential expression of 206 genes as compared to PA14, the gene expression profile of the two other mutants, ΔfliC and ΔflgK, differed only in the expression of 49 and 47 genes, respectively (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The gene expression profile of the ΔfliC mutant differed only in the expression of 49 genes compared to PA14 under standard LB culture conditions.
source: While the ΔmotABCD exhibited a differential expression of 206 genes as compared to PA14, the gene expression profile of the two other mutants, ΔfliC and ΔflgK, differed only in the expression of 49 and 47 genes, respectively (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The gene expression profile of the ΔflgK mutant differed only in the expression of 47 genes compared to PA14 under standard LB culture conditions.
source: While the ΔmotABCD exhibited a differential expression of 206 genes as compared to PA14, the gene expression profile of the two other mutants, ΔfliC and ΔflgK, differed only in the expression of 49 and 47 genes, respectively (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The three motility mutants shared 20 genes which were differentially expressed in comparison to PA14 under planktonic growth conditions.
source: The three motility mutants shared 20 genes, which were differentially expressed in comparison to PA14 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: A total of 2537 genes were differentially expressed in PA14 upon exposure to the eukaryotic cells when compared to planktonic in vitro growth conditions.
source: A total of 2537 genes were differentially expressed in PA14 upon exposure to the eukaryotic cells when compared to planktonic in vitro growth conditions.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text based on RNA sequencing data.

claim: 647 genes were induced in RAW264.7 cells upon bacterial contact with PA14 compared to uninfected host cells.
source: Eukaryotic transcriptional profiling revealed an activation of the RAW264.7 cells by P. aeruginosa with 647 genes induced (false discovery rate (FDR) ≤ 0.05) upon bacterial contact with PA14 compared to uninfected host cells.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text based on RNA sequencing data.

claim: Genes induced in RAW264.7 cells upon PA14 contact included genes located in the TNF-, NF-κB-, and MAPK-signaling pathways.
source: These included genes located in the TNF-, NF-κB-, and MAPK-signaling pathways, as well as those responsible for the expression of TLRs, and cytokine responses (Figure 3B).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: All three motility mutants induced host responses that were similar to those seen with PA14.
source: All three motility mutants induced host responses that were similar to those seen with PA14.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text based on RNA sequencing data.

claim: 31.5% (438 genes) of the overall 1392 genes that were differentially expressed upon infection were shared by all strains (ΔfliC, ΔflgK, ΔmotABCD and PA14).
source: Of the overall 1392 genes that were differentially expressed upon infection with either a motility mutant or PA14, 31.5% (438 genes) were shared by all strains (ΔfliC, ΔflgK, ΔmotABCD and PA14), while only 3.3% (46 genes) were exclusively regulated by the motility mutants and 5% (70 genes) exclusively by PA14 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The RAW264.7 macrophage genes leading to either PIP2 or PIP3 activation were expressed at lower levels upon infection with the individual motility mutants in comparison to PA14.
source: The RAW264.7 macrophage genes leading to either PIP2 or PIP3 activation were expressed at lower (albeit none significant) levels upon infection with the individual motility mutants in comparison to PA14 (Figure 5A).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The complementation of PIP3 restored the uptake of the ΔfliC mutant to wild-type levels.
source: The complementation of PIP3 restored the uptake of the ΔfliC mutant to wild-type levels and significantly increased the uptake of ΔflgK and ΔmotABCD strains (Figure 5B)
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The complementation of PIP3 significantly increased the uptake of ΔflgK and ΔmotABCD strains.
source: The complementation of PIP3 restored the uptake of the ΔfliC mutant to wild-type levels and significantly increased the uptake of ΔflgK and ΔmotABCD strains (Figure 5B)
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The putative spermidine synthesis operon was expressed at significantly lower levels in the motility mutants in comparison to PA14 upon host-cell contact.
source: The putative spermidine synthesis operon, PA14_63110, PA14_63120, PA14_63130, as well as arnT, which encodes a 4-amino-4-deoxy-L-arabinose transferase responsible for masking the immunogenic 4'-PO42- group of the lipid A molecule, were expressed at significantly lower levels in the motility mutants in comparison to PA14 upon host-cell contact (Figure 4).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 4.

claim: arnT was expressed at significantly lower levels in the motility mutants in comparison to PA14 upon host-cell contact.
source: The putative spermidine synthesis operon, PA14_63110, PA14_63120, PA14_63130, as well as arnT, which encodes a 4-amino-4-deoxy-L-arabinose transferase responsible for masking the immunogenic 4'-PO42- group of the lipid A molecule, were expressed at significantly lower levels in the motility mutants in comparison to PA14 upon host-cell contact (Figure 4).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 4.

claim: The genes encoding proteins involved in spermidine synthesis were expressed at a higher level in PA14 upon host-cell contact as compared to its planktonic growth in rich medium conditions.
source: Interestingly, the genes encoding proteins involved in spermidine synthesis were expressed at a higher level in PA14 upon host-cell contact as compared to its planktonic growth in rich medium conditions, whereas the spermidine synthesis genes were not differentially expressed (or were even expressed at lower levels) in the three motility mutants under the same conditions.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text based on RNA sequencing data.

claim: The spermidine synthesis genes were not differentially expressed (or were even expressed at lower levels) in the three motility mutants upon host-cell contact.
source: Interestingly, the genes encoding proteins involved in spermidine synthesis were expressed at a higher level in PA14 upon host-cell contact as compared to its planktonic growth in rich medium conditions, whereas the spermidine synthesis genes were not differentially expressed (or were even expressed at lower levels) in the three motility mutants under the same conditions.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text based on RNA sequencing data.

claim: Genes involved in pyoverdine biosynthesis were significantly enriched among the more highly expressed genes in all motility mutants upon host-cell contact.
source: Furthermore, genes involved in pyoverdine biosynthesis were significantly enriched among the more highly expressed genes in all motility mutants upon host-cell contact (Figure 4).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 4.

claim: The levels of TNF-α and IL-6 were significantly increased in all three motility mutants in comparison to PA14 in infected RAW264.7 and BMDM cells.
source: Screening of the supernatant of infected RAW264.7 and BMDM cells for the production of TNF-α and IL-6 revealed that the levels of these cytokines were significantly increased in all three motility mutants in comparison to PA14 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1)
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Exogenous addition of spermidine to the growth medium during infection experiments did not alter the phagocytic uptake of PA14.
source: Exogenous addition of spermidine to the growth medium during infection experiments did not alter the phagocytic uptake of PA14 (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Spermidine concentrations of 10 µM significantly increased the phagocytic uptake of the ΔfliC and ΔflgK mutants.
source: However, spermidine concentrations of 10 µM significantly increased the phagocytic uptake of the ΔfliC and ΔflgK mutants, while it did not have an effect on the uptake of the ΔmotABCD strain (Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Spermidine did not have an effect on the uptake of the ΔmotABCD strain.
source: However, spermidine concentrations of 10 µM significantly increased the phagocytic uptake of the ΔfliC and ΔflgK mutants, while it did not have an effect on the uptake of the ΔmotABCD strain (Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Addition of spermidine to the bacteria during the infection experiments was crucial as sole priming of either bacteria or host cells prior to infection did not provide a significant effect.
source: Of note, addition of spermidine to the bacteria during the infection experiments was crucial as sole priming of either bacteria or host cells prior to infection did not provide a significant effect (Figure 6B).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: The addition of spermidine induced Akt phosphorylation.
source: The addition of spermidine was uncovered to induce Akt phosphorylation, while Akt phosphorylation was not induced in untreated controls (Figure 6C).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: The ΔPA14_63120 deletion mutant produced strongly reduced levels of membrane-associated spermidine as compared to PA14.
source: As measured by HPLC-MS, the ΔPA14_63120 deletion mutant produced strongly reduced levels of membrane-associated spermidine as compared to PA14 (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: The ΔPA14_63120 mutant strain was significantly less phagocytosed by RAW264.7 cells in comparison to PA14.
source: In line with our hypothesis that the induction of bacterial spermidine production triggers phagocytic uptake, the ΔPA14_63120 mutant strain was significantly less phagocytosed by RAW264.7 cells in comparison to PA14.
evidence: This finding is stated in the text based on experimental data.

claim: Phagocytic uptake of the ΔPA14_63120 mutant by RAW264.7 macrophages could be restored to wild-type levels following the exogenous addition of spermidine.
source: Phagocytic uptake of the ΔPA14_63120 mutant by RAW264.7 macrophages could be restored to wild-type levels following the exogenous addition of spermidine (Figure 7).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 7.

claim: The addition of norspermidine restored the phagocytic uptake of the non-spermidine producing mutants at comparable levels.
source: Of note, also the addition of norspermidine (Bolard et al., 2019) restored the phagocytic uptake of the non-spermidine producing mutants at comparable levels (Figure 7 and Figure 7—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 7 and Figure 7—figure supplement 2.

claim: Motile bacteria respond differently to the presence of host cells and induce a gene expression program that determines the subsequent host response.
source: We found that motile bacteria respond differently to the presence of host cells and induce a gene expression program that determines the subsequent host response.
evidence: This is stated as a key finding in the Discussion section.

claim: The pathogen is equipped with a set of PAMPs such as the flagellum which, if present, is recognized by the host.
source: The pathogen is equipped with a set of PAMPs such as the flagellum which, if present, is recognized by the host.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the Discussion section.

claim: As a direct response to the presence of host cells the pathogen expresses further traits adding a new level of complexity to the crosstalk between them.
source: However, as a direct response to the presence of host cells the pathogen expresses further traits adding a new level of complexity to the crosstalk between them (Figure 8).
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the Discussion section and illustrated in Figure 8.

claim: Differences in motility impact phagocytic uptake rather than adherence.
source: It seems that differences in motility, rather than in adherence, impact phagocytic uptake.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the adherence assay results.

claim: Calcium transport systems and the signaling pathway leading to the production of PIP2 and PIP3 were activated in the host cell upon infection with PA14.
source: Our dual-sequencing approach revealed that calcium transport systems and the signaling pathway leading to the production of PIP2 and PIP3 were activated in the host cell upon infection with PA14.
evidence: This finding is stated in the Discussion based on the dual-sequencing data.

claim: Both calcium transport and PIP2/PIP3 pathways are known to be involved in phagocytosis.
source: Both pathways are known to be involved in phagocytosis, and a lack of their activation in the non-motile strains could explain the lower phagocytosis rates (Booth et al., 2001; Nunes and Demaurex, 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The non-motile variants are lacking a factor to stimulate PIP3 activation and calcium transport.
source: Our findings suggest that the non-motile variants are lacking a factor to stimulate PIP3 activation and calcium transport.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the findings in the Discussion.

claim: Strains with impaired motility or lack of flagella exhibit altered expression of genes involved in the biosynthesis of bacterial surface structures exclusively upon host-cell contact.
source: The transcriptional profiling of P. aeruginosa revealed that strains with impaired motility or lack of flagella exhibit altered expression of genes involved in the biosynthesis of bacterial surface structures. Of note, the motility variants differentially expressed genes encoding these structures exclusively upon host-cell contact and not under standard lab (LB or BM2 growth) conditions.
evidence: This finding is stated in the Discussion based on the transcriptional profiling data.

claim: A membrane-associated spermidine biosynthesis operon has been previously connected to antibiotic resistance.
source: A membrane-associated spermidine biosynthesis operon, which has been previously connected to antibiotic resistance (Johnson et al., 2012), was expressed at significantly lower levels in all motility mutant strains compared to PA14 wild-type upon host-cell contact.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Externally added spermidine was able to activate the Akt-pathway.
source: We furthermore demonstrate that externally added spermidine was able to activate the Akt-pathway, restoring the level of phagocytosis of the flagellar mutants and of a P. aeruginosa strain incapable of producing spermidine (ΔPA14_63120).
evidence: This finding is stated in the Discussion based on experimental data.

claim: Spermidine induced a transcriptional pattern in the host cell which was similar to that of a PA14-infected host cell.
source: We show that spermidine itself induced a transcriptional pattern in the host cell, which was similar to that of a PA14-infected host cell and involves triggering of global phosphorylation cascades (Bennetzen et al., 2012).
evidence: This finding is stated in the Discussion based on transcriptional profiling data, with a citation supporting the phosphorylation cascade aspect.

claim: Spermidine as a polyamine has been shown to mimic the effect of Ca2+ activation.
source: Spermidine as a polyamine has been shown to mimic the effect of Ca2+ activation (Koenig et al., 1983; Toninello et al., 2004), modulate immune responses (Latour et al., 2020; Theoharides, 1980) and trigger phagocytosis (TranVan Nhieu et al., 2004).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to previous literature.

claim: Polyamine depletion has previously been shown to result in increased expression of LPS-induced proinflammatory genes.
source: Furthermore, polyamine depletion has previously been shown to result in increased expression of LPS-induced proinflammatory genes, coinciding with our findings of an enhanced production of TNF-α and IL-6 in the motility mutants (Van den Bossche et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature and connects it to the current findings.

claim: Both the production of spermidine and the expression of ArnT are governed by the two-component system PmrAB.
source: Interestingly, both the production of spermidine, and the expression of ArnT are governed by the two-component system PmrAB (Gooderham et al., 2009; McPhee et al., 2006) which is located on the same operon as PA14_63120.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: PmrAB was downregulated upon host-cell contact in the mutant strains to the same extent as arnT and the spermidine biosynthesis operon.
source: PmrAB was downregulated upon host-cell contact in the mutant strains to the same extent as arnT and the spermidine biosynthesis operon.
evidence: This finding is stated in the Discussion based on the transcriptional profiling data.

claim: In E. coli, the PmrAB homolog is known to regulate motility genes.
source: In E. coli, the PmrAB homolog is known to regulate motility genes (Sperandio et al., 2002), and the Legionella pneumophila PmrAB appears to fine-tune flagellar gene expression in a negative feedback loop (Al-Khodor et al., 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The Legionella pneumophila PmrAB appears to fine-tune flagellar gene expression in a negative feedback loop.
source: In E. coli, the PmrAB homolog is known to regulate motility genes (Sperandio et al., 2002), and the Legionella pneumophila PmrAB appears to fine-tune flagellar gene expression in a negative feedback loop (Al-Khodor et al., 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: PhoPQ regulates the arn operon.
source: Upon host-cell contact PmrAB as well as a second two-component regulatory system, PhoPQ, which regulates the arn operon (Gooderham et al., 2009) and PA14_63120 (Bolard et al., 2019), were affected in the motility mutants.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: PhoPQ regulates PA14_63120.
source: Upon host-cell contact PmrAB as well as a second two-component regulatory system, PhoPQ, which regulates the arn operon (Gooderham et al., 2009) and PA14_63120 (Bolard et al., 2019), were affected in the motility mutants.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: PhoQ is regulated by the PmrAB two-component regulatory system.
source: PhoQ, is regulated by the PmrAB two-component regulatory system (McPhee et al., 2003) and was previously shown to affect twitching motility, biofilm formation, attachment and cytotoxicity in human lung epithelial cells (Gooderham et al., 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: PhoQ was previously shown to affect twitching motility, biofilm formation, attachment and cytotoxicity in human lung epithelial cells.
source: PhoQ, is regulated by the PmrAB two-component regulatory system (McPhee et al., 2003) and was previously shown to affect twitching motility, biofilm formation, attachment and cytotoxicity in human lung epithelial cells (Gooderham et al., 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: In Salmonella, PhoQ is activated within acidified phagosomes and host tissues.
source: In Salmonella, PhoQ is activated within acidified phagosomes and host tissues (Prost and Miller, 2008) and both two-component systems are activated by Ca2+ and Mg2+ limiting conditions (Guragain et al., 2016; McPhee et al., 2003).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Both PmrAB and PhoPQ two-component systems are activated by Ca2+ and Mg2+ limiting conditions.
source: In Salmonella, PhoQ is activated within acidified phagosomes and host tissues (Prost and Miller, 2008) and both two-component systems are activated by Ca2+ and Mg2+ limiting conditions (Guragain et al., 2016; McPhee et al., 2003).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: If a motile bacterium hits a cell, changes in bacterial motility in response to the physical barrier may entail altered ion fluxes across the bacterial cell membrane.
source: Since their activation is dependent on motility and the presence of a host cell, one might speculate that if a motile bacterium hits a cell, changes in bacterial motility in response to the physical barrier may entail altered ion fluxes across the bacterial cell membrane.
evidence: This is stated as speculation in the Discussion.

claim: Changes in pericellular ion homeostasis might serve as a stimulus to activate the two-component systems and the production of polyamines.
source: Changes in pericellular ion homeostasis might serve as a stimulus to activate the two-component systems and the production of polyamines, which are subsequently perceived by the host cell, thereby inducing phagocytosis.
evidence: This is stated as speculation in the Discussion.

claim: A centrifugation step was used to ensure comparable cell-to-cell contact of motile and non-motile bacterial cells.
source: We ensured comparable cell-to-cell contact of motile and non-motile bacterial cells by including a centrifugation step to establish bacterial contact with the adherent eukaryotic cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This describes a methodological approach used in the study.

claim: The ΔfliC and ΔflgK strains exhibited a similar profile of cell lysis as PA14 in the dual-sequencing experimental set-up.
source: In this experimental set-up, the ΔfliC and ΔflgK strains exhibited a similar profile of cell lysis as PA14 (see Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: The pathogen-to-host mapping ratio of RNA sequencing data was comparable among infections with PA14 and the three motility mutants.
source: Furthermore, the pathogen-to-host mapping ratio of RNA sequencing data was comparable among infections with PA14 and the three motility mutants (Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This finding is stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: Switching the medium from LB to cell culture medium did not induce the same differential gene expression profile between ΔfliC and PA14 as host-cell contact.

claim: PA14_63110 and PA14_63120 from the spermidine synthesis operon had a Spearman correlation coefficient ≥0.8 with 24% of the PIP3 genes.
